comment: Vreta's prefabs (file name without .prefab) that pipeline/arborist.py's name rule cannot match to an Arborist catalogue label. null = leave it out. 'species' is the lower vegetation (palette prefabs), 'trees' the planted trees. The pines, firs, oaks and poplars 03-07 are the very same models in Arborist (identical first-LOD size); the birches, elms, the generic broadleaf, the smallest poplar and the three lower-vegetation entries have no like-for-like model, and those choices are first guesses to be judged on screen. treeSettings / plantSettings cap how bright the leaf and bark tints may be (see arborist.py apply_look): Arborist's defaults (0.8-1.0) are far too bright under this course's light; the values follow WaterfrontGC_GSP's (birch 0.36, oak and poplar about 0.5, pine 0.6-0.7, saturation left at 1). lodFactor: the detailed model is kept this many times further out; the simpler distance models of the broadleaves are a few large leaf cards, each lit on its own, which mottles the crowns at 50-150 m (seen in Arborist 2026-10-12, where the quality setting's LOD bias is 0.7).
vsp_comment: Hybrid: the full-model trees of these prefabs (parts of prefab names) stay in the course's own VSP, because Arborist has no model as good (Forst's oaks and birches; Arborist's birches are SpeedTree models that cannot be tinted as needed). Unity must draw the same list: golfmap.vsp.trees on=true keep=<this list>. Their background trees still go to Arborist as billboard-only copies, through the 'trees' mapping.
outerKeep_comment: Marcus 2026-10-13: the horizon forest need not draw every tree, and less the further out. Bands by distance outside the course boundary [metres or null = beyond, share kept], for the billboard-only trees (arborist.py trees --surfaces). Half of all outer billboards showed no difference in the forest wall from three viewpoints and no measurable frame-rate gain either.
billboardBeyondM_comment: The far rule of arborist.py trees --surfaces: a tree both further than outsideOob outside the course boundary and further than fromPlay from the playing field (rough, semi, fairway, green, tee, bunker, wherever they lie: the range and the club's holes outside the layout count) is a billboard only; every tree inside the boundary is a full model (until 2026-10-14 either distance alone made a billboard, which put billboards beside the range tee). Marcus 2026-10-13: 40 m was too aggressive, 80 m.
vegeSettings_comment: Written into the file's VSProSettings.vegeSettings, which GSPro's Arborist system runs with (only keys the file has). PlantDistance (Marcus 2026-10-14): 350 -> 250 m saved 0.6 ms a frame at tee 1 (live in GSPro, main-thread CPU: the system culls fewer cells) with no visible difference from tee 1, the hole 4 tee and hole 6; trees stay full models to PlantDistance + AdditionalTreeMeshDistance (563 m). Omberg 2026-10-16 (Marcus): the course is open and one sees further, so PlantDistance 300: the bushes draw to all of it (renderDistance 1), the small ground plants to 0.5 of it (150 m), and everything thins out from 40 % of its distance (falloffStart) instead of ending in a line.
forstRing_comment: SWITCHED OFF 2026-10-13 (the key is renamed forstRing_off; rename it back to use it): no radius gave a frame-time gain, the birch swap shows, and Marcus finds the Forst oaks better lit in the course's VSP than as Arborist's Oak__ items. The ring rule of arborist.py trees --surfaces (ForstRing; Marcus 2026-10-13): the course's own full-model trees (the 'vsp' prefabs, Forst's CTI oaks and birches, the most expensive thing on the course) stand only on the playing field (rough, semi, fairway, green, tee, bunker; not deep rough) and within playM metres of it. Further out, and still inside the far rule, the same tree at the same position, rotation and height is a full model drawn by Arborist: the species 'replace' names for its prefab (keys are prefab file names or parts of them, the whole name wins, then the longest part; values as in 'trees'). minM widens the ring per prefab (part of a prefab name -> metres): Arborist has no birch but the SpeedTree S7_European_White_Birch, which Marcus accepts only from about 30 m from the play, so the birch ring is max(playM, 30). The oaks become Arborist's Oak__* items, which are the very same Forst meshes (identical first-LOD sizes and triangle counts) under Arborist's DEC shader with one leaf tint (treeSettings, match Oak__: #a0acc4, measured against the Forst oaks in GSPro to within 2 %, lodFactor 1 as the course's items); there is no bare-crowned Oak__, so tall_bare becomes the slimmer Oak__medium. Positions that leave the course's VSP go to data/arborist/<course>-vsp-far.json: Unity golfmap.vsp.trees.trim restore=true, then file=<that>. Remove this key and the behaviour is the plain far rule. Variants built and measured 2026-10-13 (playM 15, 30, 45): docs/gspro/arborist.md.

treeSettings.note: 2026-10-12: visually tuned in Arborist at close and medium range. Remove the leaf texture's yellow/olive colour variation and supply a uniform green tint; keep its shading and texture detail. The course's Arborist postprocessing lift.w was also raised from -0.20678772 to -0.03 to retain dark-leaf detail; scene lighting is unchanged. Billboard calibration is unchanged.

2026-10-18 (Marcus, in Arborist Ultra beside the beeches and an oak): darker leaves and a darker, warmer trunk than the calibrated #9fa5a9 / barkCap 0.7, whose trunk looked unnatural. Of four steps he found #868c90/#6e6862 and #73797c/#58534e both good; this one measured as the beech (crown luma 57/42 sunlit/back-lit against beech_05's 54/46), the other darker than every neighbour (49/34).
2026-10-18: calibrated at 1.362 for the old leaf tint #9fa5a9; scaled by the new tint's 0.85 until the billboard is measured again (calibrate.py billboards).

2026-10-13: Forst's oaks as Arborist's own items (forstRing). Tint measured in GSPro against the course's CTI Forst oaks from 22 m, June sun: crown mean 80/84/56 against 79/83/57. lodFactor 1 as the course's VSP items of the same meshes. The billboard (beyond the Arborist tree distance) is not calibrated.

plantSettings.comment: Hazel's leaf texture is dark: under the common tint it drew near black in GSPro from every side (2026-10-13). Tried live with veg.material.

trees_comment: 2026-10-18 (Marcus, Arborist Ultra lineup): Omberg's beech and elm are Arborist-only species. Their Unity stand-ins (the palette's 'beech' = the two CESimgolf elm prefabs, 'elm' = the plain Elm prefab, all hidden in the course's VSP) each share their trees between the Arborist models in the list, by position; the Unity size fit picks the stand-in, then each tree is sized to its lidar stem. Grouped by model height: the tall stand-in (Elm4-Tall, 26.6 m) takes the tall models (21-28 m), the shorter one (Elm-Split, 17 m) the 15-21 m ones. Beech: NatureManufacture's large beeches 03-05 and three DA Forest broadleaves; elm: the S7 American elm (darkened, see treeSettings) and CESimgolf's three vase-shaped Tall Fanned oaks. Arborist has no CESimgolf elm, and own prefabs cannot be added to it.
species_comment: Prefab_billberry_04 (the tall bilberry) is left out and the ferns are made small: NatureManufacture's grass-shader plants light their back faces as fronts, so from the sun's side a big bilberry bush or fern frond is white (seen in Arborist and GSPro 2026-10-12; the cure, _BackFaceMirrorNormal, is not among the values Arborist stores).
